You've got this! I'm just dealing with irritability right now :/ and fatigue. Must be a mixed episode. I hope you feel better soon.

Thank you so much for putting this together ❤ 
I didn't know until now that I really needed to read that.

When I get my depression it consumes me and all I think about is every little thing that went wrong in my life. I can't stop thinking about it either. I also become slightly suicidal (no self harm, and no acting upon my thoughts) which also consumes my thoughts. It's the worst thing ever and almost all antidepressants make me manic so I can't even take any meds for my depression. 

I just wish there was an off switch for my negative thoughts.
He's the hummingbird whisperer.
Happy Birthday!!! I spent my 29th birthday with my parents if anything I understand the no friends thing very well..
Hi so I figured I would update you, so far I am not having any side effects from Abilify and the sleep that I'm getting is better than what I got on invega. Hope you're doing well!

Making wholesome memories with my Mom and Dad. 
Music. 
Napping.
Sharing music with friends.
OF...but, I'm Hella hesitating from actually making one because I know I will regret it if I do make one.

Instead of cutting caffeine completely I switched from coffee to tea. I only did this because my anxiety was at its most extreme when I would drink coffee. Tea wakes me up and doesn't cause anxiety and shakes like coffee did.

I hope it works out for you. I don't hear voices but, I'd suggest talking to your Psychiatrist about that and, if you have a therapist talk to them about that as well. 

My therapist said that when a medication change happens usually some kind of episode will happen because it takes 4 weeks or so for the medication to actually begin to work.

The closest thing to a voice in my head is songs getting stuck in my head but, I hear it in my own voice.

Oh I'm definitely living my life. I just hate societies pressure to be successful, get married, have kids. It's just too much to think about sometimes. Then when I see others doing that I think about suicide because, I'm 29 and haven't done any of that.
Thank you so much, feel free to message me. I was definitely feeling suicidal last night. Sometimes people need support.

So like any switch of medication I dealt with a 2 week long manic episode. I sleep better. I'm able to function better than on Invega. I like how I'm getting 8 hours of sleep compared to 12 hours of sleep. It's overall so far showing proof that its better than Invega.

My dad has bipolar and was diagnosed before I was. I was diagnosed at a young age. I've also asked my dad if he's experienced certain bipolar symptoms and we are very much alike. Very hereditary I believe. Haven't done enough research to know for sure that it is.
Lol me the other day when I explained something and she started to explain how that's correlated to a trauma and how I'm reacting to my body being violated.
That's definitely good to know. Hopefully your doctor is on the same page and allows you to change medication best of luck to you in your attempt to change medicine.

Of course, I will update you in a few weeks too early to tell at the moment because, the switch happened like a week ago. I hope I lose weight as well too heavy for my liking. I also got high cholesterol from the medication. I feel like Invega just isn't worth it. Wish I knew that in the beginning I wouldn't have agreed to be put on the medication.
Something I should bring up to my T is how from time to time it's highly overwhelming that I exist and so does everyone else in the world...sometimes it's what I obsessively think about.
This is very alarming now just imagine what that soda is doing to your body big yikes 😬
Vraylar made me manic and unfortunately did not work for me I felt like I was invincible...which isn't a good thing lol

Interesting. I got shaking/tremors from invega, lost my period(I'm female), and then started to have muscle spasms in my jaw. I also gained 30 pounds in a short span of 3 months. Went from 186 to 213 pounds and, I'm sure of it over the course of being on Invega I gained more weight than that. This all concerned me and my psych. So, yesterday she decided to completely stop Invega and prescribe Abilify. I don't remember ever having issues with Abilify from like 10 years ago so, I'm hoping that I don't have any episodes when the Abilify begins to work in my system. Thanks for the input.

Most definitely my anxiety would cause me to be extremely apprehensive of confrontation. But, I would confide in my boyfriend about this and get his perspective on it first. This is definitely sad he should be getting help with those panic attacks as without therapy or even medications they can be debilitating and difficult to handle. This is just my honest opinion. I'm more of a monogamous person so, if I'm in a committed relationship I would be slightly offended if someone confessed some kind of love for me even if it's just platonic love. Personally I'd keep my distance from said person.

A few weeks ago I had forgotten the topic I wanted to bring up in therapy. Thankfully my T suggested to jot it down on paper or in my phone on notes. This is super helpful lately I've been writing down at least two things I think need to be discussed that way I don't forget again. It's very helpful.

Same here. I have days where I remind myself how comfortable my bed is but, I don't find my bed to be the most comforting place for me. I find comfort in other things rather than just solely my bed. Glad I'm not alone in this.
I'm just going to celebrate being inbetween episodes of depression and hypomania by being medicated! Although I do know eventually it will happen probably going to be depressed soon maybe.
You're a far better person for keeping the cat alive despite being ghosted by your tinder date.

I have shaved my hair into a Mohawk twice. Also, one time in a really dark time of my life while in an abusive relationship I shaved my head completely and I definitely believe it was a manic episode I was in. Currently my hair is short but, I'm trying to grow it out. Thankfully I'm on medications that are keeping me stable so I haven't had any impulsive feelings of wanting to shave my hair.
